transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I came in because this has been getting really hard to ignore, especially with work. I plan conventions and events, so I’m around people a lot more now, and there are always photos being taken or posted after things. And I keep getting stuck on this one part of my face that looks uneven to me—like in pictures especially, it’s all I can see.

Other people say they barely notice anything, or they’ll say, “You look fine,” but that honestly doesn’t really help, because when I look at the photo, my eyes go straight to it every single time. I’ll zoom in and stare at it, and then I feel like everyone else must be seeing it too, even if they say they don’t. It’s just been taking up so much space in my head that I figured I should talk to someone about it.
How does this concern about your face affect your daily life beyond work events—does it come up when you’re not in photos, like when looking in mirrors or thinking about your appearance generally?

Yeah… it definitely comes up outside of the actual events too, but I think the photos are what made it worse, if that makes sense. Like, ever since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, I started noticing it more and more, and now it’s like my brain just goes straight to that one uneven-looking part of my face.

Even if I’m not at work, if I see a picture someone took or even just think about how I might look to other people, I’ll get stuck on it. And people keep telling me they barely see anything, which should make me feel better, but it doesn’t really land. I keep thinking, “Okay, but I can see it, so how are they not seeing it?” It’s just hard to stop focusing on it once I notice it.

When you think about how you look, is your main concern specifically about this uneven part of your face, or do you also worry about other aspects of your appearance, like your skin, weight, or other features?

It’s mainly that one uneven part of my face. Like, I know everyone has little things they don’t love, but this is the thing my mind goes to over and over. Especially in photos—I’ll see a picture from work or an event and even if the whole photo is normal, my eyes just immediately go to that spot, and then I can’t really see anything else.

I wouldn’t say it’s my weight or my skin or, like, my whole appearance in general. It’s more specific than that. It’s this uneven-looking part, and the frustrating thing is people keep saying they barely notice it, or that it’s not a big deal, but I’m sitting there thinking, “How can you not see it?” Because to me it feels really obvious. And since I’m in front of people more at work now, it’s like I’m constantly aware of the possibility that someone is looking at it or that it’ll show up in a photo again.

Does this concern about the uneven part of your face cause you distress or affect other parts of your life, like avoiding social situations, spending a lot of time checking your appearance, or feeling anxious about how others see you?

Yeah… it does. I mean, I wish I could say it was just me being annoyed by a bad photo or something, but it’s started actually messing with things I need to get done.

Like at work, I had this planning deadline—part of it involved event materials, and there were photos and layouts and things where my face was included or visible, and I just got completely stuck on how I looked in them. I kept checking it and comparing versions and zooming in, and then trying to decide if I should ask for a different image or if that would seem weird, and then I’d tell myself to just move on, but I couldn’t really move on. And because of that, I actually missed part of the deadline. Not the whole event or anything, but enough that it caused problems and I felt really embarrassed.

And now even regular vendor calls or meeting prep take longer than they should, because I’ll be thinking about whether I’m going to be seen on camera, or whether something with my image is going to come up, or I’ll lose time trying to make sure I look… I don’t know, less uneven, I guess. It’s frustrating because the work itself is already busy, and I know what I’m supposed to be doing, but this concern kind of hijacks my attention. So yes, it’s definitely affecting me beyond just feeling bad about it.

latest_inference.note: The patient's concern is specifically about a perceived defect in physical appearance (asymmetry of the face), which is not observable to others and causes significant distress and impairment in functioning, particularly related to work and attentional focus. This presentation is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). Other candidates (F40.00, F32.9, F43.22) are ruled out due to the absence of predominant panic, depressive, or generalized anxiety symptoms.
